stories.summary: The Department of Energy overstepped when it ordered an aging coal-fired power plant in Michigan to stay open past its planned retirement date last year, a federal court ruled on Friday. Fed-funds traders are putting 64% odds that the Fed will do the same next week (arbitrage alert: the chances on Kalshi are a bit lower ). But the ECB’s only job is to manage inflation, while the Fed has a trickier dual task of managing both prices and employment, and so is keeping an eye on a labor market stuck in a “low hire, low fire” defensive equilibrium. Global central banks would prefer to move their interest rates together to avoid warping investment flows and currency markets. (Back in 1986, a Fed compromise was struck to let Germany and Japan cut first.) The post-Covid responses to inflation and, now, slower growth have upset that lockstep instinct as central banks tend to their own economies. — Liz Hoffman
